newsitem.title: USA: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates jump in week--FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates jump in week--FHLMC.

text.p: The average commitment rates on U.S. 30- and 15-year fixed-rate mortgages jumped upward in the week ending January 10, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp said on Thursday.
The 30-year interest rate rose 18 basis points to an average 7.85 percent in the week from 7.67 percent the previous week, while the 15-year climbed 17 basis points to 7.35 percent from 7.18 percent.
But adjustable-rate mortgages inched down to an average 5.54 percent from 5.56 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.08 percent, the 15-year 6.59 percent, and the ARM 5.45 percent.
"Mortgage rates followed the capital markets upward on news that the economy is stronger than expected, once again raising fears of inflation," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.

"The employment report due out tomorrow will influence next week's mortgage rate figures," Van Order added. "If this report supports indications of strong economic growth, we will see interest rates rise even further."
On Friday the Labor Department will issue U.S. December employment data. Earlier Thursday it said that producer prices rose 0.5 percent last month.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans in the week, both up from 1.7 percent the previous week. They charged 1.4 percent on the ARM, unchanged from last week.
